paper_title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting. When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory. We introduce MIST, an evaluation that separates the change from the memory it should leave behind. The model first sets the scene while the change stays hidden, and only later is asked to show it, with leakage before that point kept under control. This separation locates the bottleneck: the model sets the scene but does not carry out the instructed change. The same gap appears in general memory evaluations. On that basis we propose M3-Agent (Make the Missing Move), which recursively revises the details of the input instruction so that the model successfully carries out the requested instruction. Relative to the baseline, it more than triples the MIST reveal score. On the benchmarks, WRBench's score T rises by 26.1% and MBench-T's score U by 52.7%. The method meets the problem from the execution side: it shows what the frozen model can do once the move is stated, and it sets a stricter baseline.

They do show that the model can already carry out many missing changes once the instruction names them. The method meets the problem from the execution side: it shows what the frozen model can already do once the move is stated. This paper makes three contributions  (Fig. 1)  . (1) MIST, an evaluation that scores whether the scene is set, whether the hidden change leaks, and whether it is finally shown, so missing change is not reported as forgetting (34). Related Work low memory score can come from failed persistence, wrong state update, or missing operation that never makes the state observable. The three lines of work below each report one total. Video generators as world models. Extended literature map and positioning This section records the wider 20242026 literature used to bound the papers claims. Entries are grouped by the question they answer, rather than presented as evidence for one aggregate notion of memory. What enables long and persistent rollouts? Diffusion and latent-video foundations establish the rendering lineage [Ho et al., 2020, Blattmann et al., 2023, Team Wan, 2025], while physical-AI platforms broaden the world-model framing [NVIDIA et al., 2025]. Recent systems address exposure bias, out-of-sight dynamics, bounded memory, and revisit stability through selfconditioned training or explicit state [Huang et al., 2025b, Duan et al., 2026b, Team et al., 2026, Xu et al., 2026b]. Omnimodal enterable worlds, controlled action-memory probes, and longhorizon audiovisual story generation extend the same line [Zhang et al., 2026b, King et al., 2026, Duan et al., 2026a]. Agent-driven and embodied evaluations further test whether actionconditioned worlds remain usable over long objectives [Ding et al., 2026, Wang and Li, 2026, Yang et al., 2026, Liu et al., 2026]. EntityBench separately measures recurring entities across multi-shot gaps [He et al., 2026b]. Long-horizon generators and packing systems also appear in the main related work [Wu et al., 2024b, Xiang et al., 2024, Zhu et al., 2024, Garcin et al., 2026, Wang et al., 2026]. These works motivate long-horizon memory, but architectural success in one protocol does not resolve MISTs execution-versus-persistence ambiguity. Which benchmark dimensions are adjacent to MIST? WorldBench and IntPhys 2 isolate physical concepts and object permanence, whereas EWMBench and VBench 2.0 separate scene, motion, semantics, and intrinsic faithfulness [Upadhyay et al., 2026, Bordes et al., 2025, Yue et al., 2025, Zheng et al., 2025]. Understanding suites separate endpoint answers from continuous tracking [Yu et al., 2026, Chen et al., 2026b, Han et al., 2026b]. LongVideoBench and MLVU test

ChronoMagic-Bench separates amount of change from temporal coherence, and T2VPhysBench evaluates physical laws with manual judgments [Yuan et al., 2024, Guo et al., 2025]. Adjacent temporal and physical suites include TC-Bench, T2V-CompBench, OSC-Bench, YoCausal, PhyGenBench, and VideoPhy2 [Sun et al., 2024, Han et al., 2026a, Xie et al., 2026, Meng et al., 2024, Bansal et al., 2025]. MIST instead fixes target state and asks whether the generated operation makes that state judgeable after an opaque gap. How has video generation been refined at test time? Reward gradients and human-feedback rewards improve video generation through learned objectives [Prabhudesai et al., 2024, Liu et al., 2025b]. GenMAC and Prompt-A-Video use collaborative or preference-aligned prompt revision [Huang et al., 2024, Ji et al., 2024]. ScalingNoise, VISTA, RAPO++, and ImagerySearch broaden search over noise, prompts, candidates, or evaluators [Yang et al., 2025a, Long et al., 2025, Gao et al., 2025, Wu et al., 2025]. LatSearch and noise-trajectory search move selection inside diffusion inference, while GEARS diagnoses and recycles candidates [Zhao et al., 2026, Ramesh and Mardani, 2025, He et al., 2026a]. M3-Agent is not generic test-time search. Its contribution is an operation-constrained response to delayed-reveal diagnosis, and its score-aware selection remains an oracle coverage analysis. What can automated video evaluators establish? VBench and EvalCrafter established multidimensional evaluation beyond single perceptual totals [Huang et al., 2023, Liu et al., 2023b]. VideoScore, AIGV-Assessor, LOVE, and UVE learn or organize fine-grained human-facing quality or task judgments [He et al., 2024, Wang et al., 2024, 2025, Liu et al., 2025c, Li et al., 2024]. VideoGen-Eval decomposes prompts into checkable questions, while WorldJen and RAVEN-Eval study rubric design, score compression, ordering, and confidence [Yang et al., 2025b, Inbasekar et al., 2026, Jia et al., 2026]. CLIP-style alignment and vision-centric VLMs provide useful readers [Radford et al., 2021, Liu et al., 2023a, Tong et al., 2024], but no one reader is treated here as ground truth for latent state. This is why MIST reports gate-specific judgments, held-out reread, and explicit disagreement with official scorers. Embedding-centric vision learners and generators, and cycle-consistent text-guided image editing, sit adjacent to the representation and prompt-revision tools used above [Xu et al., 2025, 2026a, 2023].
